newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson Multimedia has 3.0 bln ffr '96 loss - paper.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Multimedia has 3.0 bln ffr '96 loss - paper.

text.p: Thomson Multimedia (TMM), the 100 percent owned consumer electronics unit of state company Thomson SA, is set to report a net attributable loss of 3.0 billion francs for 1996, the Les Echos newspaper said.
This compares with a 1995 loss of 1.09 billion.
The group, slated for privatisation, is also expected to report an operating loss of 500 million against a profit of 352 million in 1995.
For the first half of the year, TMM already posted a 3.0 billion franc net loss and 1.2 billion operating loss, indicating it made some improvement in the second half.
TMM is reorganising its activities, having taken a 1.2 billion franc charge in the first half, to return to profit.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Wednesday TMM would get a capital injection in the next few weeks.
This recapitalisation, seen at 10 billion francs, will cut financing costs by 600 million francs.
TMM expects to be structurally profitable in 1998 when it will receive payments on patents of its GE/RCA U.S. unit under the terms of the orginial acquisition deal with General Electric Corp.
